questions.explanation: Find faces that end up opposite (they can never be seen together): cross & target, dot & square, plus & ring. Then check the order around a corner. Only B shows three faces that really meet at a corner in that order (top, left, right going anticlockwise: cross, plus, square).

distractors.A: the cross and the target are on opposite faces, so they can never be seen together
distractors.C: the right three faces, but in mirror-image order around the corner
distractors.D: these faces do meet, but not in this order around the corner

questions.explanation: A letter seen in the same picture as M is on a face touching M, so it can't be opposite. The letters next to M are A, G. Work out where the remaining letters must go: the face opposite M is S.

distractors.A: A is seen next to M in one of the pictures, so it can't be opposite
distractors.C: not opposite
distractors.D: G is seen next to M in one of the pictures, so it can't be opposite

questions.explanation: Find faces that end up opposite (they can never be seen together): cross & ring, dot & target, plus & square. Then check the order around a corner. Only B shows three faces that really meet at a corner in that order (top, left, right going anticlockwise: target, ring, plus).

distractors.A: the target and the dot are on opposite faces, so they can never be seen together
distractors.C: the right three faces, but in mirror-image order around the corner
distractors.D: these faces do meet, but not in this order around the corner

questions.explanation: Find faces that end up opposite (they can never be seen together): cross & dot, plus & target, ring & square. Then check the order around a corner. Only D shows three faces that really meet at a corner in that order (top, left, right going anticlockwise: ring, dot, plus).

distractors.A: the right three faces, but in mirror-image order around the corner
distractors.B: these faces do meet, but not in this order around the corner
distractors.C: the ring and the square are on opposite faces, so they can never be seen together

questions.explanation: Find faces that end up opposite (they can never be seen together): cross & target, dot & square, plus & ring. Then check the order around a corner. Only A shows three faces that really meet at a corner in that order (top, left, right going anticlockwise: ring, square, cross).

distractors.B: these faces do meet, but not in this order around the corner
distractors.C: the right three faces, but in mirror-image order around the corner
distractors.D: the ring and the plus are on opposite faces, so they can never be seen together

questions.explanation: Count the cubes layer by layer, or column by column (heights 2 2 2; 2 1 0; 2 0 0). There are 11 cubes. A 3 × 3 × 3 cube has 27 cubes, so Sam needs 27 − 11 = 16 more.

distractors.A: that is the number of cubes already there

Only C shows three faces that really meet at a corner in that order (top, left, right going anticlockwise: cross, target, square).

distractors.B: these faces do meet, but not in this order around the corner
distractors.D: the right three faces, but in mirror-image order around the corner

distractors.A: the right three faces, but in mirror-image order around the corner
distractors.B: the ring and the square are on opposite faces, so they can never be seen together
distractors.D: these faces do meet, but not in this order around the corner

questions.explanation: Find faces that end up opposite (they can never be seen together): cross & square, dot & target, plus & ring. Then check the order around a corner. Only B shows three faces that really meet at a corner in that order (top, left, right going anticlockwise: plus, cross, target).

distractors.A: the plus and the ring are on opposite faces, so they can never be seen together
distractors.C: the right three faces, but in mirror-image order around the corner
distractors.D: these faces do meet, but not in this order around the corner
